item.title: Montana Tech Names First Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer in Montana University System
item.description:
# Montana Tech Names First Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer in Montana University System ![Chad Okrusch](https://www.mtech.edu/_images/people/chad-okrusch1.jpg)Recognizing the transformative impact of emerging technologies on higher education and industry, Montana Technological University has appointed Professor Chad Okrusch, Ph.D. to serve as the university’s first chief artificial intelligence officer.
As chief artificial intelligence officer, Okrusch will lead Montana Tech’s strategic integration of artificial intelligence across campus, ensuring that students, faculty, and staff are equipped to navigate, utilize, and shape the future of AI responsibly.
- Establishing safe frameworks for AI use involving sensitive materials, data privacy, and academic integrity. - Supporting faculty with resources, workshops, and assignment models that use AI to strengthen critical thinking rather than replace cognitive work. - Partnering with IT and administrative units to pilot AI workflows for routine processes while mitigating data security risks.
"Artificial intelligence is not simply a set of tools to be adopted; it is a disruptive sociotechnological system that often feels untethered and out of our control,” said Okrusch.

item.title: AI Play Summer Camp Brings Young Tech Innovators to Queens
item.description:
Nearly two dozen Charlotte-area middle schoolers spent a week diving into artificial intelligence and computer science during the inaugural AI Play Summer Day Camp at Queens University of Charlotte.
The weeklong program from July 20-24 brought rising sixth through eighth graders to campus for an immersive exploration of artificial intelligence and computer science.
The rapid growth of artificial intelligence formed a central theme of the camp’s discussions.
As artificial intelligence continues to transform the modern world, Goslen said, initiatives like AI Play help bridge the gap between abstract computer science concepts and everyday life.
